from.place: The ordinary and compact-support cohomology complexes in the two displayed Frobenius composites: their canonical coefficient-stage realization and coefficient enlargement.

title: Coefficient enlargement preserves the prescribed cohomology arrow
statement: With the canonical stage functors R and endpoint comparisons B of [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-realization-data], take Pair objects K,M, a common stage L and an enlargement L <= N. For every f: K.toStage(L) -> M.toStage(L), the arrow B(K,N).hom ; R_N(tr(f)) ; B(M,N).inv equals B(K,L).hom ; R_L(f) ; B(M,L).inv in D(Omega). Here tr is the specified associator-conjugated transition of [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category]. This is an equality of pre-quotient arrows; no descended functor or Frobenius isomorphism is asserted.

source.place: (1.1.10)-(1.1.14), coefficient localization and transport of cohomology; extracted coefficient-realization step of the parent.

proof.text: Factor the existing endpoint comparison as p inverse followed by A applied to q, using the explicit canonical factors. Its equality with the original construction is proved componentwise; no realization data is changed. Insert the explicit functor associators between the whiskered factors; their components are identity arrows. Package these specified factors in a constructed private record, so the abstract categorical identities specialize without reopening their geometric constructions. The scalar data are explicitly constructed together with the proved tensor cocycle; the full record then adds the specified rational functors and comparisons.

Apply the rational cocycle and the scalar-and-size tensor cocycle. Naturality of p inverse moves q past the intermediate coefficient comparison. Map the rational cocycle through A_N; the scalar cocycle cancels the resulting field associator and gives the endpoint tower identity. This categorical pasting is a complete Lean proof in realizedStageComparison_coherence.

Use the endpoint tower identity at K and M. Expand tr into inverse source associator, transition of f and target associator. The image associators cancel, naturality of the realized stage comparison moves f past that comparison, and inverse endpoint maps cancel. This proves the original coefficient-enlargement equality without a descended functor.

lean.statement:
theorem frobeniusCohomologyRealization_transport
    (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (hl : l ≠ D.p)
    (Y₀ : Over (Spec (.of D.k₀))) [LocallyOfFiniteType Y₀.hom] [QuasiCompact Y₀.hom]
    [IsSeparated Y₀.hom]
    (Ω : Type v) [Field Ω] [Algebra ℚ_[l] Ω] [IsAlgClosure ℚ_[l] Ω]
    (c₀ : Compactification Y₀.hom) (compact : Bool)
    (K M : generalAlgebraicallyClosedConstructibleCategory l Ω (D.geometricFiber Y₀).left)
    (L N : Index l Ω) (hK : K.stage ≤ L) (hM : M.stage ≤ L) (h : L ≤ N)
    (f : K.toStage hK ⟶ M.toStage hM) :
    (frobeniusCohomologyRealizedComparison D l hl Y₀ Ω c₀ compact K N (hK.trans h)).hom ≫
        (frobeniusCohomologyRealizedStage D l hl Y₀ Ω c₀ compact N).map
          ((stageSystem l Ω (D.geometricFiber Y₀).left).tr h f) ≫
        (frobeniusCohomologyRealizedComparison D l hl Y₀ Ω c₀ compact M N
          (hM.trans h)).inv =
      (frobeniusCohomologyRealizedComparison D l hl Y₀ Ω c₀ compact K L hK).hom ≫
        (frobeniusCohomologyRealizedStage D l hl Y₀ Ω c₀ compact L).map f ≫
        (frobeniusCohomologyRealizedComparison D l hl Y₀ Ω c₀ compact M L hM).inv
